title: Shallow Decorator Forests (Subclassitis of Composition)
pattern: Constructing nested towers of generic, shallow decorators to inject simple operational concerns like logging, auditing, or metrics tracking.
why_bad:
*   **Compilation Complexity:** In languages like Rust, deep towers of generic wrappers cause monomorphization explosion, slowing down compilation and bloating binary sizes.
*   **Opaque Interfaces:** Finding where actual execution occurs requires stepping through multiple wrapper layers, turning debugging into a chore.
detection: Nesting or wrapping of struct generic layers $\ge 3$ deep, where the wrapper structs contain no unique domain data and only perform pre/after forwarding calls.
counterexample: **Middleware Interceptors:** Utilizing a single, unified interceptor chain or middleware registration framework is valid.
source: Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Section 4.6 "Classitis" & McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 6.4 "Reasons to Create a Class".
